INFORMATION  The total mark for this paper is 30.  Each correct answer will score one mark.  Any rough working should be done on this question paper.
In a planned economy, what will determine the allocation of scarce resources?

options.A: a mixture of private and central decision making
options.B: the decisions of central government
options.C: the forces of demand and supply
options.D: the revenue generated from direct and indirect taxes

questions.questionText: A key concept in classifying goods is whether a good is rival or non-rival. Which good is rival in consumption?

options.A: an ice cream
options.B: street lighting
options.C: a radio broadcast
options.D: the internet

questions.questionText: What is a normative statement?

options.A: A firm receiving a government subsidy will increase the supply of a good.
options.B: Negative externalities are the most serious market failure.
options.C: A rise in incomes will lead to a rise in demand for normal goods.
options.D: A rise in the additional rate of income tax will decrease the incentive to work.

questions.questionText: The diagram shows an economy’s production possibility curve (PPC). The economy has moved from X to Y. capital Y P goods X Q O R S consumer goods What can be deduced from the diagram?

options.A: Current living standards have fallen.
options.B: The economy has become more efficient.
options.C: There has been a rise in unemployment.
options.D: There has been an opportunity cost of OR consumer goods.

options.A: decreases elastic

questions.questionText: What is an example of a product in joint demand with a smartphone?

options.A: an alternative brand of smartphone
options.B: a personal computer (PC)
options.C: headphones that can be used with a smartphone
options.D: the metals used in the manufacture of a smartphone

questions.questionText: A product has a high price elasticity of supply. What might explain this?

options.A: It has a high opportunity cost.
options.B: It has a non-perishable nature.
options.C: It is classed as an inferior good.
options.D: It is classed as a luxury good.

questions.questionText: What is likely to affect the position of the demand curve for tickets to pop concerts but not the position of the supply curve?

options.A: a change in incomes of potential customers
options.B: a change in price of tickets to the concerts
options.C: a change in rents charged by venue owners
options.D: a change in seating capacity of concert venues

questions.questionText: The table shows Lee’s and Yim’s price elasticity of demand for restaurant meals and cinema tickets. Lee Yim restaurant meals –1.2 –0.8 cinema tickets –0.7 –0.3 There is a rise in the price of both products. What can definitely be concluded after these price changes?

options.A: Restaurant owners will receive more income.
options.B: Lee will spend more money on both products.
options.C: Yim will spend more money on both products.
options.D: Cinema owners will receive less income.

questions.questionText: A government fixes a maximum price for a product in order to increase its consumption. What would be the likely outcome of such a policy?

options.A: Consumption will fall if the maximum price is above the current equilibrium price.
options.B: Consumption will rise if the maximum price is below the current equilibrium price.
options.C: Production will fall if the maximum price is above the current equilibrium price.
options.D: Production will fall if the maximum price is below the current equilibrium price.

What is a transfer payment?

options.A: the advertising expenditure of a firm
options.B: the allowance given by a parent to their child while at school
options.C: the rent paid to a land owner by a tenant farmer
options.D: the wage paid to a worker in the government service

questions.questionText: What best illustrates the process of privatisation?

options.A: a single private shareholder acquires complete control of an organisation
options.B: the purchase of government bonds by private sector commercial organisations
options.C: the purchase of shares in a private company
options.D: the transfer of public sector assets to the private sector

questions.questionText: What defines a progressive tax?

options.A: Low-income earners pay the same proportion of income in taxes as high-income earners.
options.B: Low-income earners pay a lower proportion of income in taxes than high-income earners.
options.C: Low-income earners pay less in taxes than high-income earners.
options.D: Low-income earners pay more in taxes than high-income earners.

questions.questionText: An increase in what will shift the aggregate demand curve in an economy to the right?

options.A: budget deficit
options.B: consumer savings
options.C: general price level
options.D: interest rate

questions.questionText: Which effect of inflation is described as redistributive?

options.A: the improvement in the terms of trade
options.B: the deterioration in the balance of trade
options.C: the inconvenience of frequently changing prices
options.D: the loss of purchasing power for people on fixed incomes

questions.questionText: In which situation will a country’s terms of trade improve?

options.A: Its total value of imports rises less than its total value of exports.
options.B: Its volume of imports rises less than its volume of exports.
options.C: The prices of its imports rise by less than the prices of its exports.
options.D: The value of its external payments rises by less than the value of its external receipts.

questions.questionText: What is likely to happen if there is a fall in the international value of a country’s currency?

options.A: a rise in the foreign currency price of its exports
options.B: a rise in the volume of its exports
options.C: a fall in the domestic currency price of its imports
options.D: a fall in the domestic price level

questions.questionText: From the same quantity of factors of production, country X and country Y each produce the following units of output. country sugar textiles X 30 20 Y 40 10 Which statement is correct?

options.A: Country X has absolute advantage in the production of both goods.
options.B: Country X has comparative advantage in the production of sugar.
options.C: Country Y has absolute advantage in the production of textiles.
options.D: Country Y has comparative advantage in the production of sugar.

questions.questionText: Following a 10% depreciation in the $ value of the £ sterling, a UK exporter leaves the $ price of the goods it sells in the US market unchanged. Other things being equal, what will be the effect on the revenue measured in sterling obtained by the manufacturer from its sales in the US?

options.A: It will increase.
options.B: It will decrease.
options.C: It will be unchanged.
options.D: It will depend on the elasticity of demand for the manufacturer’s good in the US.

questions.questionText: The diagram shows the effect of introducing a tariff on a product. price domestic supply P world supply plus tariff P world supply domestic demand O quantity What determines the producer surplus that the tariff generates for domestic producers?

options.A: the price elasticities of domestic supply and demand
options.B: the tariff rate and the price elasticities of both domestic demand and supply
options.C: the tariff rate and the price elasticity of domestic demand
options.D: the tariff rate and the price elasticity of domestic supply

questions.questionText: Which government policy is most likely to cause expenditure switching that will benefit a country’s current account?

options.A: increasing import quotas
options.B: increasing income tax allowances
options.C: increasing spending on unemployment benefits
options.D: increasing subsidies to domestic firms

questions.questionText: Which type of economic policy is likely to be considered the most effective by a government that has greater income equality as its primary aim?

options.A: fiscal policy
options.B: international trade policy
options.C: monetary policy
options.D: supply side policy
